title: 1959 AHSME Problem 49
statement: For the infinite series \[ \begin{aligned} &1-\dfrac12-\dfrac14+\dfrac18\\ &{}-\dfrac1{16}-\dfrac1{32}+\dfrac1{64}\\ &{}-\dfrac1{128}-\cdots, \end{aligned} \] let \(S\) be the (limiting) sum. Then \(S\) equals:

solutions.text:
Group the series as \[ \begin{aligned} S={}&\left(1-\frac12-\frac14\right)\\ &+\left(\frac18-\frac1{16}-\frac1{32}\right) +\cdots. \end{aligned} \] The first block is \(\frac{1}{4},\) and successive blocks form a geometric series with ratio \(\frac{1}{8}.\) Hence \[ S=\frac{\frac{1}{4}}{1-\frac{1}{8}}=\frac27. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Group the terms in consecutive blocks of three
Each block is \(\frac{1}{8}\) times the preceding block
